bank.explanation: 'I can design' is a skill; 'menu design for local cafés' is a service a client can buy.

bank.question: Bilal has a full-time job search and three evening hours. Which promise to a client is most professional?
options: A delivery date that fits his real available hours
The fastest delivery on the platform, to win the order
No delivery date, so he can work whenever he likes
Delivery 'today', then a quick apology if it is late
bank.explanation: Realistic promises that fit your time protect your reputation from the first project.

bank.question: On the demand and skill grid, a freelancer is excellent at calligraphy but few clients search for it. What is the best plan?
options: Make it the only service and wait for demand to grow
Stop practising it completely because it has no value
Keep it as a side interest and start with a higher-demand skill
Claim it is in high demand in every proposal
bank.explanation: High skill with low demand is a niche hobby box. Start where clients already pay, and keep the hobby alive on the side.

bank.question: Which description of freelancing is most accurate?
options: A guaranteed monthly income from online platforms
A job where a platform manager plans your day
Running a small service business with its own duties and freedoms
Easy money that needs no planning or records
bank.explanation: Freelancers gain freedom but must find clients, manage time, keep records and handle payment themselves.

bank.question: Ayesha writes, 'I can do anything you need.' Why is this weak for a beginner?
options: It gives the client no clear result or reason to trust her
Platforms do not allow the word 'anything'
It is too short to appear in any search
Clients only hire people who say 'expert'
bank.explanation: Vague offers are hard to judge. A specific result for a specific client builds trust faster.

bank.question: A beginner has watched tutorials on a skill but never completed a real piece of work in it. Which action best fits professional standards?
options: Sell it now at expert level and simply learn the skill during orders
List it as the main service with invented reviews
Ask clients to pay first and then learn the skill
Build practice samples first, then offer it honestly
bank.explanation: Selling a skill you cannot yet deliver risks unhappy clients and poor reviews. Practise and build samples first.

bank.question: Which pairing correctly describes the two marketplace models in general terms?
options: Gig model: clients post jobs; proposal model: you publish ready-made packages
Gig model: you publish offers; proposal model: you apply to posted jobs
Gig model: only hourly work; proposal model: only fixed prices
Both models: the platform assigns work to freelancers in turn
bank.explanation: In the gig model (as on Fiverr) you set up a ready-made offer. In the proposal model (as on Upwork) clients post jobs and you apply. Both sites offer more than one way of working.

bank.question: A new client on a marketplace asks to pay Ayesha directly by bank transfer 'to save fees'. Which reply is best?
options: Politely keep the work and payment on the platform, as its rules require
Agree, because saving fees helps both sides
Agree, but only if the client pays half first
Send her bank details and phone number in the chat
bank.explanation: Many platforms forbid moving new clients off-platform. Staying on-platform also keeps the protection the platform provides.

bank.question: Bilal wants to know a platform's current fee. Which source is most reliable?
options: A popular video recorded several years ago
A message forwarded in a large group chat
The platform's own current terms or help pages
The fee another freelancer remembers paying on their first order
bank.explanation: Fees and rules vary and change. The platform's own current pages are the reliable source.

bank.question: Why do platforms not publish the exact formula for how they rank profiles in search?
options: Every profile is simply shown in the same random order to all clients
Ranking methods are their own and change over time
Search results depend only on your city
Clients choose the formula for each search
bank.explanation: Ranking methods are not fully public and are updated. Focus on what you control: quality, honesty, communication and on-time delivery.

bank.question: Which action is usually against marketplace rules?
options: Asking the client project questions in the platform's own chat
Delivering files through the delivery button
Showing samples you created yourself
Asking a relative to order your gig for a review
bank.explanation: Fake orders and reviews mislead clients and usually break the terms; accounts can be restricted for them.

bank.question: In general terms, why is payment handled through the platform rather than directly?
options: It means the freelancer never has to deliver work
It lets the platform choose the project's scope
It removes the need for any client communication
It gives both sides a level of protection under the platform's process
bank.explanation: The platform processes and releases payment under its own rules. The exact protection depends on the platform's current terms and the contract type.

bank.question: A client on a proposal-model platform posted a clear job. What gives Bilal the best chance of being noticed?
options: A first line that lists his university grades
A first line that restates the client's goal
A copy of the same message he sent to others
A request for the client's phone number
bank.explanation: The first line shows the client you read their job. Copied messages and off-platform requests hurt your chances.

bank.question: Which profile overview opening is most client-focused?
options: I am a very passionate, creative and hard-working designer
Hello, I am new here and need my first order
Your café's menu deserves posts that make people hungry
I have many skills and can do any kind of work
bank.explanation: It begins with the client's result. The others talk only about the freelancer.

bank.question: Ayesha has no paid work. Which portfolio approach is honest and effective?
options: Practice projects she made herself, clearly labelled as samples
Attractive designs downloaded from a free images site and shown as hers
A famous agency's work with her name added
Empty, with a note asking clients to trust her
bank.explanation: Labelled practice work shows real ability without misleading anyone. Using others' work is dishonest and may break copyright and platform rules.

bank.question: Which gig element most reduces back-and-forth before work starts?
options: A very long title packed with every possible keyword the buyer might search
Clear buyer requirements listing what the client must send
A description that only talks about your hobbies
Images that show other designers' finished work
bank.explanation: Telling buyers exactly what to provide, such as logos, text or photos, lets you start quickly and avoids confusion.

bank.question: Which proposal is strongest for a job asking for a phone-friendly shop website?
options: A short reply restating the need, one matching sample, a plan and a question
A long story about his childhood interest in computers
'Dear Sir, I am expert. Check my profile. Thanks.'
A copied list of every programming language he knows
bank.explanation: Short, specific, tailored proposals with proof and a smart question stand out.

bank.question: Bilal uses an AI tool to help draft a proposal. Which practice is acceptable?
options: Letting the tool invent past clients to sound experienced
Pasting a client's private files and details into the tool without asking first
Sending the tool's first draft unchanged to every job
Checking grammar, then making sure every claim is true and fits the job
bank.explanation: Tools can help with wording, but he is responsible for honesty, fit and client privacy.

bank.question: A relative's shop agrees to let Ayesha design its posts for free in return for showing the work. How should she present it?
options: As a paid project with a large invented budget
As work for a famous brand to impress clients
As real work, shown with permission and described honestly
With a fake five-star review from the shop
bank.explanation: Real work shown with permission is a good start, but it must be described honestly.

bank.question: Which of these most damages trust on a new profile?
options: Labelling your work as practice samples
Listing your languages at an honest level
Claiming experience or qualifications you do not have
Including a clear, friendly profile photo
bank.explanation: False claims break trust when the truth appears and can break platform rules.

bank.question: Bilal's proposals get many views but almost no replies. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Send twice as many copies of the same proposal every single day
Lower his price to the lowest on the platform
Remove his profile photo to look more serious
Add a tailored insight and a closely matching sample
bank.explanation: Views mean the first line works. Low replies point to the body: tailored insight, proof and a clear next step.

bank.question: Ayesha wants Rs 50,000 a month and has about 50 paid hours a month. Before costs, fees and margin, what is her floor per paid hour?
options: Rs 500
bank.explanation: Rs 50,000 divided by 50 paid hours is Rs 1,000. This is a practice calculation; she then adds costs, fees and margin.

bank.question: Why should a freelancer count only 'paid hours' when working out an hourly floor?
options: Platforms only allow freelancers to work a fixed, set number of hours each week
Proposals, messages and learning take time that clients do not pay for
Clients always pay for every hour spent on the laptop
Paid hours are the same as the hours in a working week
bank.explanation: Much of a freelancer's time is unpaid. Dividing your goal by all hours would set the floor too low.

bank.question: A client asks for 'some improvements, whatever is needed' on an old website. Which pricing approach is usually wisest?
options: Hourly, or a small paid first step to clarify the scope
One low fixed price for everything, just to make sure of winning the job
Free work until the client decides what they want
A fixed price with unlimited changes included
bank.explanation: Unclear scope makes fixed prices risky. Hourly work or paid discovery protects you while you define the job.

bank.question: A client says your fair quote is too high. Which response best protects your business and the relationship?
options: Cut the price by half and keep the same scope
Offer a smaller scope that fits their budget at your normal rate
Tell them other freelancers are dishonest
Stop replying and wait for them to give up
bank.explanation: Changing the scope, not your value, keeps your rate fair and still helps the client.

bank.question: A happy client offers a five-star review if you give a discount on the next order. What should you do?
options: Accept, as long as the review is long, detailed and positive
Accept, and ask for reviews from their friends too
Ask them to post the review from several accounts
Decline the trade and ask only for honest feedback
bank.explanation: Reviews must be honest. Trading discounts for ratings misleads clients and usually breaks platform rules.

bank.question: Which message best handles a likely one-day delay?
options: Silence until the client asks where the work is
Delivering half-finished work on the original day
An early note with the reason in brief, a new date and an apology
A long message blaming the client's slow internet
bank.explanation: Early, honest updates with a new realistic date keep trust even when plans change.

bank.question: Why should platform fees and payment charges be part of your price calculation?
options: They are always added on top for the client to pay
They are exactly the same on every platform and never change
They only matter for projects above a certain size
They reduce what you receive, and they vary and change
bank.explanation: Check the current terms for the platform and payment method you use, and price so you still earn above your floor.

bank.question: The scope is one label with two revision rounds. Which request is a change request rather than a revision?
options: Making the brand name slightly bigger
Switching to the agreed darker green
A matching design for a second product
Correcting a spelling mistake on the label
bank.explanation: A new item is new work and can be quoted separately. The others change delivered work inside the scope.

bank.question: What is the best first step when a kind client keeps adding 'small' extras outside the agreed scope?
options: Keep doing them free so the client stays happy
Thank them, explain it is new work and quote a price and time
Refuse rudely and close the project immediately
Do them slowly without explaining anything
bank.explanation: Polite, clear change requests protect your time and the relationship.

bank.question: For a direct client outside a marketplace, which item matters most to include in a short written agreement?
options: Deliverables, price, payment timing, revisions and deadlines
Your favourite colours and design style
A list of every client you worked with before
The client's personal social media passwords
bank.explanation: These details prevent most disputes. For large or unusual work, seek qualified advice; never ask for passwords.

bank.question: A client in another country asks who owns the final designs. What is the most responsible approach?
options: Say she owns everything and can resell it freely
Agree usage in writing and check the applicable law or seek advice
Say nothing and hope it never comes up
Copy an ownership clause from a random website
bank.explanation: Ownership and usage should be agreed in writing, and laws differ, so check the law or seek qualified advice for unusual cases.

bank.question: Using the urgency and importance grid, how should 'update portfolio with new case study' usually be treated?
options: Urgent and important: drop all client work to do it right now
Urgent but less important: rush it in five minutes
Important but not urgent: schedule a fixed time for it
Neither urgent nor important: never do it
bank.explanation: Growth tasks rarely have a deadline today, so schedule them before they are forgotten.

bank.question: A client sends an angry message demanding unlimited changes or a full refund, though the agreed scope was delivered on time. What is the best sequence?
options: Stay calm, cite the scope, ask what is wrong, offer included revisions, then use platform support if needed
Reply in anger at once, then leave a bad review for the client
Agree to unlimited changes, then quietly stop replying
Refund at once without asking what went wrong
bank.explanation: A calm, factual approach gives the fairest chance of resolution and leaves a clean record for any dispute.

bank.question: Which habit best protects you if a dispute happens on a marketplace project?
options: Agreeing important changes only by phone call, with nothing written down
Sending final files by personal e-mail only
Deleting messages once the project starts
Keeping key messages and deliveries on the platform
bank.explanation: A clear record on the platform helps its support or resolution process understand what was agreed and delivered.

bank.question: A client has not sent the text needed for a website for a week. What is the most professional step?
options: Write the text yourself without asking the client
Deliver the website with empty pages on the deadline
Send a polite reminder explaining how the delay moves the deadline
Cancel the project without telling the client why
bank.explanation: Client inputs affect your timeline. A polite reminder that links inputs to the deadline keeps things fair and clear.

bank.question: Which statement about receiving international freelance payments is accurate?
options: Methods and rules vary and change, so check current terms and the law
One method is free, instant and available to everyone
Using a relative's account avoids every legal question
Informal routes are fine if the exchange rate is better
bank.explanation: Use legal channels in your own name and check the current terms of providers and official guidance.

bank.question: Bilal's income is growing and he is unsure about tax registration and returns. What is the most responsible action?
options: Rely on advice from an anonymous social media post
Assume there are never any rules for freelancers
Stop recording income so there is nothing to report
Check current FBR guidance and consider a qualified tax adviser
bank.explanation: Tax rules are set by law and can change. Official guidance and qualified advice, with good records, are the safe approach.

bank.question: A new direct client overpays and asks you to forward the extra to a friend by mobile wallet before the payment clears. What is happening?
options: A normal, accepted practice for international website and design projects
A likely overpayment scam that can leave you out of pocket
A bonus you should keep without telling anyone
A platform fee that you are required to pay
bank.explanation: The original payment can be reversed, and any money you send is lost. Accept only the agreed amount through a verified method.

bank.question: Which message is the clearest red flag?
options: 'Pay a small fee first and we will send you work'
'Could you share two samples similar to this style?'
'What would your timeline be for ten posts?'
'Can we start with a small order on the platform?'
bank.explanation: Genuine clients pay you for work. Being asked to pay for the chance to work is a classic scam.

bank.question: Which monthly routine best supports tax and bank questions later?
options: Estimating the year's income from memory in the last week
Saving statements and recording income, fees and expenses each month
Keeping only screenshots of positive client reviews
Recording income only when a bank asks about it
bank.explanation: Regular, simple records make filing, answering bank questions and planning much easier.

bank.question: What most strongly builds a freelancer's personal brand over time?
options: Changing your name and niche every month
Posting the same advertisement in every group daily
Copying a successful freelancer's profile word for word
A clear focus, honest results and kept promises
bank.explanation: A consistent focus, real case studies and a reputation for reliability bring repeat clients and referrals.
